title: “The Circuit” is currently selling through June 29th via New York The...
transcript: it's an immersive silent disco ballet performance taking inspiration from a classic play to explore messy relationship dynamics in modern day. the Circuit is a dance theatre piece where you're guided through the streets and parks of Dumbo wearing wireless headphones that play the original score which blends EDM with a more melancholic style of music you also hear pre-recorded dialogue that the former is silently act along to which works better than it sounds like it would the audience is told that you're always welcome to dance at any time but you don't have to. on the surface level the show is relatively simple but entertaining; the dancing is great, the music is cool, and you can enjoy the scenery of the Dumbo waterfront. but the simplicity here is deceptive. the show left a surprisingly strong almost haunting impression on me afterward. part of that being that it's kind of a brilliant marriage of form and content. it's actually partly inspired by the 1897 play La Ronde which you might also know from the musical adaptation, Hello Again the most famous thing about it being its circular daisy chain structure where it's a series of two person scenes and the new character introduced in each scene is the one that we follow into the next until we circle back around to the first character. not only was this a logistically  smart way of structuring an experience like this it also insightfully adapts the central theme of La Ronde to modern day using this silent disco nightlife setting, it creates a surprisingly plaintive portrait of characters longing for connection, several of them bumping up against the emotional and physical boundaries of their non monogamous relationships, some of them feeling the deep ache of a situationship with blurry lines and some giving into the intoxicating heat of a fleeting moment
